front: What is the critical condition for an algebraic expression to be called a polynomial?
back:
The exponents of all variables appearing in the terms must strictly be non-negative integers (whole numbers: 0, 1, 2, 3...).
Expressions with fractional powers (like √x) or negative powers (like 1/x = x-1) are NOT polynomials.
note: Coefficients can be irrational (e.g. √2 x<sup>2</sup> is a valid polynomial).

front: What is the degree of a non-zero constant polynomial, and what is the degree of the zero polynomial?
back:
• Non-zero constant polynomial (e.g. p(x) = 5 = 5x0): Degree is 0.
• Zero polynomial (p(x) = 0): Degree is not defined.

front: What is a zero of a polynomial P(x), and how many zeroes does a linear polynomial ax + b (a ≠ 0) have?
back:
A real number k is a zero if P(k) = 0.
A linear polynomial ax + b has exactly one zero:
x = -b / a.
note: Geometrically, it is the x-intercept of the line y = ax + b.

front: Evaluate the polynomial P(x) = x3 - 10x2 + 3x - 4 at x = -1.
Find the zero of the polynomial: p(x) = (x - 2)2 - (x + 2)2.
note: From PA-2 School Exam Section C (Question 31).

front: Can a polynomial have zeroes that are not 0, and can 0 be a zero of a polynomial?
back:
Yes to both!
• Zeroes can be any real number (e.g. p(x) = 2x - 6 has zero x = 3).
• The number 0 can be a zero (e.g. p(x) = 5x has zero x = 0 since p(0) = 0).
note: Don't confuse the number 0 with the zeroes (roots) of the polynomial.
